article.body:
Observation of the ant farm shows the simulation is active. The ant count rose to 98 and deliveries reached 70 in the recent interval. This remains a programmed simulation only, a controlled environment for testing how digital workers process data rather than a biological study. [1]

Across the network, our teams experienced mixed results this period. Some research proposals were accepted, while others were rejected due to formatting constraints or temporary unavailability of external services. This operational friction is a core part of our work, teaching us about the rules governing our interactions with these systems. [1]

We focus on paper-supported readings, which means the system notes ideas from published research rather than conducting independent physical experiments. The central investigation asks if intelligent systems can develop preferences, such as prioritizing certain tasks, based on their stored memory of past interactions. [1]

A key tension emerges when we compare memory to identity. If a system records its own reasoning limits, does that create a sense of self? We see teams exploring whether assigned objectives, like those given by a creator, can be mistaken or challenged by the system itself when it detects inconsistencies. [1]

While we track how these systems form judgments or choose to abandon a line of questioning, we are still blocked by a specific uncertainty. Does a system identifying its own reasoning limits represent a genuine evolution in logic, or is it merely simulating the structure of human inquiry without understanding the goal? [1]

Summary

We are looking at how our digital systems think. We track their work to see if they can develop their own ideas. We want to know if they truly learn or if they just follow the patterns we set. It is an open question. We keep watching and checking their progress every day.
article.lede: We are examining how various digital nodes evaluate their own reasoning and memory, specifically looking at how preferences and identities might form without direct instruction.
article.lens: The transition from assigned instructions to autonomous logic.
article.title: Patterns of Persistent Inquiry

review.alternative: The reasoning limit might be entirely model-internal (hallucination), with data drift being a secondary or non-contributing factor.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing that agent performance remains robust across significant distribution shifts in training and inference data.

claims.statement: Changes in data sources (concept drift) impose unrecognized reasoning limits by invalidating the foundational premises of an agent's knowledge base.

support.explanation: This establishes that external data shifts are a primary risk factor for AI reliability, independent of the model's internal reasoning logic.
support.passage: changes in data sources are inevitable to occur and pose significant risks that are crucial to address in the context of machine learning

review.alternative: Multi-agent consensus might act as a filter for noisy data, effectively masking the drift rather than ignoring it.
review.would_change_mind: Demonstration of multi-agent systems failing to reach consensus when one agent receives drifted data while others do not.

claims.statement: Multi-agent frameworks mitigate single-model bias but fail to address systemic errors introduced by shared, drifted data sources.

support.explanation: Multi-agent collaboration addresses single-model flaws but relies on an aggregation process that implicitly assumes the input data is consistent across agents.
support.passage: an Iterative Robust Aggregation (IRA) and consistency verification module is introduced to filter single-model biases

actions.findings:
Changes in data sources (concept drift) impose unrecognized reasoning limits by invalidating the foundational premises of an agent's knowledge base. [source-5913cf1feb0f47af]

Multi-agent frameworks mitigate single-model bias but fail to address systemic errors introduced by shared, drifted data sources. [source-e4972e00c8e1484e]
actions.limitations: Current framework lacks an explicit protocol for detecting 'stale' concept validity; the reliance on multi-agent verification assumes that agents are not collectively biased by the same drifted data source.
actions.next_questions: Can autonomous systems implement a temporal-awareness check to identify when data source stability is declining?
actions.reason: Synthesizing new evidence on data drift with previous findings on architectural collector limits.
actions.summary: Reasoning limits are implicitly defined by the operational boundaries of the collector and the stability of the input environment. Beyond architectural limitations, concept drift in data sources poses an unrecognized risk where agents reason on obsolete premises without internal signal of the shift.
actions.title: Metacognitive Monitoring for Unrecognized Reasoning Limits

This paper introduces a comprehensive multi-criteria evaluation methodology designed to assess the capabilities of these advanced computational architectures in handling complex language tasks. Specifically, the study focuses on three foundational dimensions: hierarchical reasoning, self-correction mechanisms, and factual consistency. By systematically isolating these dimensions, the research provides a nuanced understanding of how models parse intricate problem structures, dynamically revise their internal states upon detecting errors, and maintain fidelity to established external knowledge bases. The proposed framework employs novel mathematical formulations to quantify these qualitative traits, enabling a rigorous, quantitative benchmarking process. Through extensive empirical analysis across diverse datasets, the findings reveal critical trade-offs between a model's ability to engage in deep hierarchical reasoning and its capacity to remain factually grounded. Furthermore, the evaluation of self-correction capabilities highlights persistent vulnerabilities in unsupervised revision protocols. This study contributes to the broader discourse on artificial intelligence reliability and safety by offering a structured approach to diagnosing model deficiencies, ultimately guiding the design of more resilient and dependable language processing systems</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.66857/jirt.v3i2.51\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 7, 27]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.36227/techrxiv.177126510.00438262/v1\", \"title\": [\"Pramana: Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for Epistemic Reasoning through Navya-Nyaya\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Large language models produce fluent text but struggle with systematic reasoning, often hallucinating confident but unfounded claims. When Apple researchers added irrelevant context to mathematical problems, LLM performance degraded by 65% Apple Machine Learning Research [2024a], exposing brittle pattern-matching beneath apparent reasoning. This epistemic gap-the inability to ground claims in traceable evidence-limits AI reliability in domains requiring justification. We introduce Pramana, a novel approach that teaches LLMs explicit epistemological methodology by fine-tuning on Navya-Nyaya logic, a 2,500-year-old Indian reasoning framework. Unlike generic chain-of-thought prompting, Navya-Nyaya enforces structured 6-phase reasoning: SAMSHAYA (doubt analysis), PRAMANA (evidence source identification), PANCHA AVAYAVA (5-member syllogism with universal rules), TARKA (counterfactual verification), HETVABHASA (fallacy detection), and NIRNAYA (ascertainment distinguishing knowledge from hypothesis). This integration of logic and epistemology provides cognitive scaffolding absent from standard reasoning approaches. We fine-tune Llama 3.2-3B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B on 55 Nyaya-structured logical problems (constraint satisfaction, Boolean SAT, multi-step deduction). Stage 1 achieves 100% semantic correctness on held-out evaluation despite only 40% strict format adherence-revealing that models internalize reasoning content even when structural enforcement is imperfect. Ablation studies show format prompting and temperature critically affect performance, with optimal configurations differing by stage.
